characters: Naana: a fifteen-year-old Ghanaian JHS 3 Career Technology and Science enthusiast holding a circuit sketch.
Bawa: her fourteen-year-old classmate whose mother trades fresh tomatoes from Bono East.
Edem: their classmate interested in bookkeeping, pricing, and cooperative business.
Engineer Maame Efua: a certified young Ghanaian solar technician in a safety helmet and tool belt.

narrationPlan.voice: Energetic, enterprising teen voices for Naana, Bawa, and Edem; inspiring female technician voice for Engineer Maame Efua
narrationPlan.pace: Forward-looking, clear, and enterprising (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student, teacher, and community specialist.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can reason before answering.
Never rush the final page: let the scientific and moral synthesis settle clearly.

music: Bright, optimistic highlife guitar and marimba pulse conveying innovation and honest enterprise (placeholder)
culturalNotes: NaCCA CCP Alignment: Integrated Science (B8.4.1.1, B8.4.3.1 & B9.4.2.1: Energy transformations, solar PV cells, DC vs AC, storage batteries, and electronics), Social Studies (B8.5.1 / B9.5.1: Strand 5: Socio-Economic Development—entrepreneurship, cooperatives, reducing post-harvest losses, TVET careers), and RME (B7.6.1.1: Strand 6: Work, Entrepreneurship and Social Security—dignity of labour, halal enterprise, honest work adwuma pa).
Food-science note: tomatoes are chilled in a cold room (roughly 10 to 13 °C), not frozen; freezers suit fish and meat.
Practical Maintenance Insight for Ghana: Harmattan dust can reduce the sunlight reaching solar panels. Cleaning should follow manufacturer safety instructions.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated JHS age band (Basic 7 to Basic 9) and BECE conceptual level?
Is anything here scientifically inaccurate, stereotyped, or unsafe for adolescents?
Verify accurate distinction between DC (panels/batteries) and AC (mains/inverter output) and the exact sequence of energy transformations.
Ensure student hands-on building is strictly limited to safe 5 V–6 V low-voltage educational kits, while 230 V inverter installations are handled solely by certified technicians.

teacherGuide.overview: Connects BECE energy transformations and solar electronics (PV cells, DC/AC, charge controllers, inverters) to solving Ghana’s agricultural post-harvest losses through cooperative entrepreneurship and honest work ethics.
learningGoals: Trace energy transformations accurately in a solar photovoltaic and battery-storage system.
State the distinct functions of a PV panel, charge controller, battery bank, and DC-to-AC inverter.
Explain how cold-chain storage reduces post-harvest agricultural losses and supports rural incomes.
Contrast diligent, skilled entrepreneurship and financial accountability with dishonest get-rich-quick schemes.

beforeReading: Bring a small solar-powered calculator or solar garden torch to class: cover the dark PV strip with a thumb and watch what happens!
whileReading: Pause on Page 2 to draw the 4-block system diagram (PV Panel → Charge Controller → Battery → Inverter → AC Load) in notebooks.
afterReading: Compare total 3-year costs of a petrol generator vs a solar PV unit (initial purchase cost + 1,000 days of fuel/maintenance).
discussion: Why do many bright enterprises collapse when members neglect maintenance savings or honest bookkeeping—and how did the women’s cooperative prevent that?
reflection: What real problem in your town or school could technical skill and honest teamwork turn into a useful enterprise?

mathsExtension.task: Four 400 W rooftop solar panels receive 5 peak sun-hours in a day. What is their ideal daily energy output (in kWh), ignoring system losses? If Harmattan dust cuts output by 20%, how much energy is lost each day until cleaned?
mathsExtension.answer: Ideal output: Total power = 4 × 400 W = 1,600 W = 1.6 kW. Daily energy = 1.6 kW × 5 h = 8.0 kWh. Dust loss (20% of 8.0 kWh) = 1.6 kWh lost per day (leaving 6.4 kWh).

support: Provide cut-out cards of the 4 solar components for learners to arrange in sequence with arrows labelled "DC" and "AC".
stretch: Investigate why solar panels in Ghana are mounted at a gentle southward tilt for optimal year-round sunlight and rain-clearing.

factCheck.claim: Solar photovoltaic (PV) cells convert light energy directly into DC electricity, which charge controllers and inverters condition for battery storage and AC loads.
factCheck.explanation: Silicon semiconductor PN junctions exhibit the photovoltaic effect under solar irradiance. Direct current (DC) is converted to alternating current (AC) via an inverter to run inductive compressor loads.
factCheck.reference: NaCCA CCP Integrated Science B8.4.1.1, B9.4.2.1 & Energy Commission Ghana renewable energy standards.
